ov: Small, round, short-tailed rodents of the Arctic tundra and the main prey of most Arctic predators. They do not hibernate: in winter they live in tunnels under the snow, with rest areas, toilet areas and nests. Their numbers boom and crash roughly every four years.
rg: In or near the Arctic across North America, Europe and Asia, including Norway and Siberia.
df: Mostly mosses and grasses, plus berries, leaves, shoots, roots, bulbs and lichens.
fx: A flattened claw on each front foot helps it dig in snow.
